Exam Name: Screening Mammography, Bilateral (Digital)
Reason for Exam / Clinical Indication: Routine screening mammogram; no new breast complaints. Patient is 52 years old with no personal history of breast cancer. Last mammogram 1 year ago.
Technique: Digital mammography was performed in craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) projections of both breasts. Computer-aided detection (CAD) was utilized.
Comparison Study: Prior mammogram from 10/25/2023 (Evergreen Medical Center).

Findings:
BREAST COMPOSITION: The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses.
RIGHT BREAST: No suspicious masses, architectural distortion, or clustered microcalcifications are identified. Skin and subcutaneous tissues are unremarkable.
LEFT BREAST: No suspicious masses, architectural distortion, or clustered microcalcifications are identified. Skin and subcutaneous tissues are unremarkable.
AXILLAE: No axillary lymphadenopathy is noted bilaterally.

Impression:
1. No evidence of malignancy. BI-RADS Category 1: Negative.
2. Heterogeneously dense breast tissue.

Recommendation:
Routine annual screening mammogram in one year.
